Fix what the output names. Move the tasks it touches to in_progress with UpdateTask while you work and to tested once their tests pass; leave the rest of the board as it is.

Reproduce the failure with a run narrowed to the test the output names, fix it, then run that test again and build its project. The whole sweep runs again as soon as you stop with every task tested, so stopping on a fix you have not run costs another one.

CodeOutline on the failing test's file gives the line each test starts on: Read that test's range rather than the whole file.

What earlier tasks left:
- Remembering what the person settled [tested]: src/agent/memory/memories.ts: MemoryScope, MEMORY_CAP (50); projectMemoryDir(cwd, home) = the Claude Agent SDK's own default auto-memory folder, ~/.claude/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/memory/, used as our own explicit notes folder (not the SDK's hidden auto-memory tool, which is turned off); userMemoryFile(home) = ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the one file user-scope memory lives in as a `## Memories` section; MemoryEntry, DroppedNote; rebuildProjectIndex(dir) rebuilds MEMORY.md from the note files on disk oldest-by-mtime-first and enforces the cap (the "notes are the truth" rebuild the next tasks can reuse); enforceUserMemoryCap(text) dedupes/caps the Memories section's bullets; MemoryContract (SessionHooks) wired into every session via src/session-engines.ts composeHooks, watches Write/Edit and hands back the chat-line instruction; memoryWritingInstructions(cwd, home) is the prompt text wired into both engines' chat system prompts (src/agent/openai-session/system-prompt.ts buildSystemPrompt, and src/session-engines.ts startClaude's append-prompt branch). SdkSession.buildOptions (src/agent/sdk-session/sdk-session.ts) now always sets settings: { autoMemoryEnabled: false }. (files: src/agent/memory/memories.ts, src/agent/openai-session/system-prompt.ts, src/session-engines.ts, src/agent/sdk-session/sdk-session.ts, test/memories.test.ts, test/system-prompt.test.ts, test/sdk-session.test.ts, plan/project-and-user-wide-memories.spec.md)
- Starting a session with what is already known [tested]: `src/agent/memory/session-context.ts`: wantsMemories(mode) = mode !== 'plan'; MemorySources = {project, user}; readMemorySources(cwd, home) reads the project's MEMORY.md and the person's whole `## Memories` section (via memories.ts's new userMemorySection); memorySection(sources) renders both into one "## What is already known" block, index-only (a project note's body is never inlined, only its index line), and states "the project note holds" on a clash, but only when both scopes have notes; withMemories(mode, systemPrompt, cwd, home) appends that block for every mode but 'plan', used as `ctx.withMemories` (new field on ModeContext, wired in mode-setup.ts's implement/code-plan/docs/file-decisions/docs-map/reconcile/cleanup cases, deliberately left out of 'plan'); chatMemorySection(cwd, home) = memorySection(readMemorySources(...)) reused by session-engines.ts's startClaude for its chat/full-access branch (both scopes, since the Claude engine's own CLAUDE.md loading excludes `user` and its auto-memory tool is off). memories.ts gained userMemorySection(text). system-prompt.ts's buildSystemPrompt (the own loop's chat prompt) now also appends the project index alongside the instruction files it already reads whole (which is where the person's own notes already reach it, so only `project` is passed there, not `user`, avoiding a second copy on that engine's side too). (files: src/agent/memory/session-context.ts, src/agent/memory/memories.ts, src/agent/session/mode-setup.ts, src/session-engines.ts, src/agent/openai-session/system-prompt.ts, test/memory-session-context.test.ts, test/mode-setup.test.ts)
- Reviewing and forgetting [tested]: memories.ts gained: listMemories(cwd, home) (rebuilds the project index from the notes on disk and reads the user's bullets, so a hand edit is always reflected — "notes are the truth" for listing); forgetMemory(scope, title, cwd, home) (deletes the note file and rebuilds the project index, or strips the matching bullet from the user's file); removeUserMemoryBullet(text, title); memoryPath(scope, file, cwd, home) (resolves a listed entry back to its absolute file). memoryWritingInstructions now also tells the model to correct a misleading note in place rather than wait for a sweep (there is none). settings-store.ts gained MemoryPort (list/forget, injected like ConfigPort/SecretPort) and SettingsStore.forgetMemory; SettingsSnapshot (protocol.ts) gained `memories: { project, user }`; FromSettingsWebview gained `open_memory`/`forget_memory`. settings-panel.ts's constructor gained a `memoryPathOf` callback used to open a memory's file with vscode.window.showTextDocument. The webview gained a "Memories" tab (memories-tab.ts, MemoryOpenedEvent/MemoryForgottenEvent in events.ts) listing both scopes with Open/Forget per entry, wired in settings-app.ts and extension.ts. 2	import { dirname, join } from 'node:path'
3	import { readOptional, replaceFile } from '../workspace-files'
4	
5	/**
6	 * Where the generated map lives and how it is put on disk. Everything under
7	 * `.agent/repo-map/` is build output: a build replaces the whole set, so an
8	 * edit a session makes there is not refused, it is lost at the next build.
9	 *
10	 * Writing goes through a staging directory and per-file renames, so a reader
11	 * opening an index while a build runs sees the previous file whole or the new
12	 * one whole, never half of either.
13	 */
14	
15	/** Workspace-relative root of the map; the form paths take in the injected summary. */
16	export const MAP_ROOT = '.agent/repo-map'
17	
18	/** The small part handed to a session at its start. */
19	export const SUMMARY_FILE = 'summary.md'
20	
21	/** Per-project type indexes; one file each, named after the project. */
22	export const INDEX_DIR = 'types'
23	
24	/** One generated file: a path relative to the map root, and the whole of its content. */
25	export type MapFile = { path: string; text: string }
26	
27	export const mapRoot = (cwd: string): string => join(cwd, ...MAP_ROOT.split('/'))
28	
29	/** Workspace-relative path of a file in the map, as the summary names it. */
30	export const mapPath = (path: string): string => `${MAP_ROOT}/${path}`
31	
32	export const summaryPath = (cwd: string): string => join(mapRoot(cwd), SUMMARY_FILE)
33	
34	/**
35	 * The bytes a file is stored as: `\n` endings and exactly one trailing newline,
36	 * so the same content renders the same on any host.
37	 */
38	export const mapText = (text: string): string => `${text.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').replace(/\s+$/, '')}\n`
39	
40	/** Code-unit order, not the host's locale: the same input has to sort the same on every machine. */
41	export const byPath = (a: string, b: string): number => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0)
42	
43	/** Sorted by path, so the set written never depends on the order it was produced in. */
44	export const sortFiles = (files: MapFile[]): MapFile[] => [...files].sort((a, b) => byPath(a.path, b.path))
45	
46	/**
47	 * Replaces the map wholesale: every file given is written, every file that was
48	 * there and is not given is removed. Files land by rename out of a staging
49	 * directory, one at a time, each replacing its predecessor in a single step.
50	 */
51	export async function writeMap(cwd: string, files: MapFile[]): Promise<void> {
52	  const root = mapRoot(cwd)
53	  await mkdir(root, { recursive: true })
54	  const staging = await mkdtemp(`${root}.tmp-`)
55	  try {
56	    const written = sortFiles(files)
57	    for (const file of written) {
58	      const target = join(staging, ...file.path.split('/'))
59	      await mkdir(dirname(target), { recursive: true })
60	      await writeFile(target, mapText(file.text), 'utf8')
61	    }
62	    for (const file of written) {
63	      const target = join(root, ...file.path.split('/'))
64	      await mkdir(dirname(target), { recursive: true })
65	      await replaceFile(join(staging, ...file.path.split('/')), target)
66	    }
67	    await prune(root, new Set(written.map((f) => f.path)))
68	  } finally {
69	    await rm(staging, { recursive: true, force: true })
70	  }
71	}
72	
73	/** Reads one file of the map by its path relative to the root; undefined when the build has not produced it. */
74	export const readMapFile = (cwd: string, path: string): Promise<string | undefined> =>
75	  readOptional(join(mapRoot(cwd), ...path.split('/')))
76	
77	/** Every file under the map root, workspace-relative to it, sorted. */
78	export async function listMap(root: string, prefix = ''): Promise<string[]> {
79	  let entries
80	  try {
81	    entries = await readdir(root, { withFileTypes: true })
82	  } catch (error) {
83	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') return []
84	    throw error
85	  }
86	  const paths: string[] = []
87	  for (const entry of entries) {
88	    const path = prefix === '' ? entry.name : `${prefix}/${entry.name}`
89	    if (entry.isDirectory()) paths.push(...(await listMap(join(root, entry.name), path)))
90	    else paths.push(path)
91	  }
92	  return paths.sort(byPath)
93	}
94	
95	/** Leftovers of an earlier build: files the new one did not produce, and the directories they emptied. */
96	async function prune(root: string, keep: Set<string>): Promise<void> {
97	  for (const path of await listMap(root)) {
98	    if (!keep.has(path)) await rm(join(root, ...path.split('/')), { force: true })
99	  }
100	  await removeEmptyDirs(root)
101	}
102	
103	async function removeEmptyDirs(dir: string): Promise<void> {
104	  for (const entry of await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
105	    if (!entry.isDirectory()) continue
106	    const child = join(dir, entry.name)
107	    await removeEmptyDirs(child)
108	    if ((await readdir(child)).length === 0) await rm(child, { recursive: true, force: true })
109	  }
110	}

questions.header: A real flake outside the reported output
questions.question: test/repo-map-files.test.ts > a_reader_during_a_build_sees_a_whole_file_never_a_partly_written_one fails most runs on its own: it re-reads a 400 KB file every millisecond, so the file is open ~99% of the time and Windows refuses the build's rename onto it (EPERM) until the retry budget runs out. It is the repo map's rule B7, not this feature's. How should it be settled?

options.label: Let the reader let go between reads
options.explanation: The test polls with a gap, as a session that reads the map once does; it still proves a reader never sees half a file, and the build's rename lands.

options.label: Make the build wait longer instead
options.explanation: Keep the test as it is and give the writer a much larger patience budget - but a reader that never lets go can still block it, so the flake only gets rarer.

options.label: Leave it alone
options.explanation: Not this feature's test; the next sweep keeps failing on it.

event.text: The sweep's reported failure was vitest worker startup, not the feature's code — and the user ruled `vitest.config.mts` belongs to the sibling session running on this feature, so I left it untouched. What I did fix is a genuine race it exposed: `test/repo-map-files.test.ts > a_reader_during_a_build_sees_a_whole_file_never_a_partly_written_one` re-read a 400 KB file with no gap, holding a handle on it ~99% of the time, so Windows refused the build's rename onto it (EPERM) until the retry budget ran out — it failed about three runs in five standalone. The reader now lets go for 25 ms between reads, as a session that reads the map once does, and the test still proves no reader sees half a file: 6/6 green on that file, `npm run typecheck` clean, and the full suite green (1416 passed, 3 skipped, 9 s). The board's three tasks are tested, with the fix recorded on "Remembering what the person settled".
